solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Show long film in empty depot

indicators.note: the film is placed inside what remains of the depot
an emptied depot has lost its contents, leaving just its outside letters

parts.note: an epic is a long, grand-scale film

explanation.surface: A long film being screened in a deserted depot.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray something in a picture or words is a synonym of to show it.

clue.text: Mark needs to complete on time

parts.note: to do a job is to complete it

explanation.surface: Someone needs a good mark to finish punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spot or point is a mark, as in a dot on paper.

clue.text: Mounting insolence very unattractive in religious traveller

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means the word climbs, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lip is informal for cheeky insolence
grim can mean very unpleasant or ugly

explanation.surface: Rising cheekiness is ugly in someone devout who travels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounting' in a down clue reverses LIP to PIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A person journeying to a shrine or holy place for devotion is the classic example.

clue.text: Conflict of meaning I'd turned up in abridgement

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the shortened form

parts.note: a contraction is a shortened form, an abridgement

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: I'd gives the letters I and D

explanation.surface: A grammarian notes a clash of sense in a shortened word such as I'd.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' means read upwards, so the pair of letters is reversed before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Two statements that clash in sense are at odds logically, a direct opposition of meaning.

clue.text: Small print run

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A short print run at a press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' looks like part of the printing phrase 'print run', but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A short fast race or dash is a run at full speed.

clue.text: In favour of period of living allowance increase

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a life is the span of time one lives
a ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies

explanation.surface: Someone supports raising a lifetime allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid multiplication or spread of something is a growth, a big rise in numbers.

clue.text: Preliminary section not requiring all of paint roller

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the words paint roller are used, buried within them

explanation.surface: An instruction for a decorating job: the early stage does not need the whole roller.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening passage of a song or book is its preliminary part, short for introduction.

clue.text: One who harasses soldiers trapped between hills

indicators.note: the troops are caught with a hill on either side of them

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor; two of them for the plural
men is a common crossword word for soldiers or troops

explanation.surface: Soldiers caught between hills face an enemy who harries them.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop of south-west England, such as on Dartmoor; the plural 'hills' supplies one on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who torments others is a persecutor, a person causing distress.

clue.text: Assistant keeping son out of the way

indicators.note: the helper holds the other letter within

parts.note: an aide is an assistant or helper
S is the usual abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An assistant keeps a son away from trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something to one side is to move it away, so the adverb means off to the side.

clue.text: One seeking ability in latest portent put out

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: The latest omen has been issued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like 'published', but it signals an anagram of LATEST PORTENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A scout looking for gifted performers or players searches for people with skill.

clue.text: Unending rage as skin removed from animal

indicators.note: with no ending, the synonym for rage loses its final letter

parts.note: fury is violent anger, rage

explanation.surface: Endless fury as an animal is skinned.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelt or hairy coat taken from a mammal is what coats and stoles are made of.

clue.text: Warns of bad outcome of beers drunk with food

indicators.note: drunk suggests the beers are in a muddled state, their letters jumbled with the food

explanation.surface: Beer drunk with a meal is a bad omen.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell trouble or have a premonition of disaster is a verb for ominous prediction.

clue.text: Twisted druid shed blood in G&S operetta

indicators.note: a twisted thing is bent out of shape, so the letters of druid are rearranged

parts.note: gore is blood that has been spilt

explanation.surface: A bent druid spilt blood in a Gilbert and Sullivan show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' turns DRUID into RUDDI. G&S is Gilbert and Sullivan, the Victorian comic opera partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruddigore is one of the Savoy comic operas written by Gilbert and Sullivan.

clue.text: Cure male beset by having a thin and high-pitched voice

indicators.note: the male letter is surrounded on both sides by the adjective

parts.words: having a thin and high-pitched voice
parts.note: a reedy voice is thin and high

explanation.surface: A treatment for a man troubled by a squeaky voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine or treatment that heals is a cure; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Ninth month with sci-fi film group

parts.note: Sept is short for September, the ninth month
E.T. is Spielberg's science-fiction film

explanation.surface: A sci-fi film shown in September.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of seven musicians or things is a specific kind of group.

clue.text: School worker sees a head in term, mostly

indicators.note: the per-person word sits inside the shortened term
mostly means all but the last letter of the word term

parts.note: each means per person, a head

explanation.surface: A school employee meets the head during term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a head' means per person, as in a pound a head; 'mostly' drops the last letter of term.
explanation.definitionFit: A classroom educator is the obvious member of staff in a school.

clue.text: Throw away turn in game

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Discarding a turn in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbers game of calling and crossing off on cards is played in halls.

clue.text: Single prominent feature introduced by most of bad porcelain

indicators.note: the two words are brought in between the remaining letters of the shortened word
most of means the last letter of bad is dropped

parts.note: single means one
a chin is a prominent facial feature

explanation.surface: A lone striking item comes with most of a bad set of china.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of bad; 'introduced by' puts the other pieces between its two remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine white ceramic made with bone ash is a type of porcelain.

clue.text: Very unpleasant royal line suffers double beheading

indicators.note: losing two heads means the first two letters are removed

parts.note: a dynasty is a line of hereditary rulers

explanation.surface: A royal house loses two of its members to the executioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffers double beheading' removes DY from DYNASTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something horrid or vile is extremely disagreeable, the adjective's everyday sense.

clue.text: Tune just lacks force

indicators.note: the word for just is missing the letter for force

parts.note: fair means just or equitable
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: A melody that is simply weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'merely' but means FAIR, which 'lacks' F.
explanation.definitionFit: A melody or song is an air, as in a folk air.

clue.text: Eminent doctor hiding studies

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A noted medic keeps his research secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning alter, the anagram signal for HIDING STUDIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone famous and respected in their field is renowned, highly regarded.

clue.text: Almost serves deer

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: does means serves or suffices, as in that does the job

explanation.definitionFit: A female deer or rabbit is called by this name.

clue.text: Maxim is remaining after tour's leader has gone

indicators.note: the first letter of tour's has departed from the word for remaining

parts.note: staying means remaining

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A traveller stays on after the tour guide has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tour's leader' is T, which 'has gone' from STAYING.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb or saying is a short pithy statement of general truth, an adage.

clue.text: Regret following unit when one's gone wrong

indicators.note: the word for regret comes after the shortened unit
gone means the letter has left the word unit

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral; one's means one has
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A soldier feels remorse after his unit takes a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's gone' removes I (Roman one) from UNIT to leave UNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something false or incorrect is not accurate, the adjective's plain sense.
